facts.fact_text: On 5 March 2007 a demonstration was held on the campus of Dicle University to protest about the conditions of Abdullah Öcalan's detention.
The demonstration on 5 March 2007 at Dicle University protested in particular about the alleged poisoning of Abdullah Öcalan by the Turkish authorities.
On 5 March 2007 a group of forty people entered the Dicle University building and asked the students to leave.
On 5 March 2007 the group of forty people held a press conference on the premises of Dicle University.
On 5 March 2007 the group of forty people chanted slogans in favour of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan on the premises of Dicle University.
On 9 March 2007 the applicant was arrested.
During questioning on 10 March 2007 at the anti-terror branch of the Diyarbakır police headquarters, the applicant denied taking part in the demonstration of 5 March 2007 at Dicle University.
During questioning on 10 March 2007 at the anti-terror branch of the Diyarbakır police headquarters, the applicant denied taking part in the funeral of 28 March 2006 and the subsequent events.
The applicant was shown photographs taken of him on 28 March 2006 during the funeral of the PKK militants.
The applicant was shown photographs taken of him on 5 March 2007 during the demonstration at Dicle University.
The applicant accepted to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had participated in the funeral of one of the PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had attended the funeral on 28 March 2006 as a religious duty.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that on 5 March 2007 he had stood in front of the Dicle University building with other students for a short while.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that his photograph must have been taken while he stood in front of the Dicle University building on 5 March 2007.
Before the judge of the Diyarbakır Assize Court on 10 March 2007, the applicant maintained that his statements to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor had reflected the truth.
In the first police video recording, the applicant was seen in a crowd next to a coffin making a 'V' sign.
In the second police video recording, the applicant was seen in a crowd with the hood of his coat on his head.
In the third police video recording, the applicant was seen applauding with other students.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant made defence submissions stating that he had attended the funeral on 28 March 2006.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant stated that he had briefly participated in the gathering at Dicle University on 5 March 2007.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant accepted that he was the person in the photographs submitted as evidence.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant stated that he did not remember making a 'V' sign but that he might have done so along with the rest of the crowd.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed, on the basis of the police video recordings and photographs extracted from those recordings, that the applicant had attended the funeral of four PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had walked in front of one of the coffins during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had made a 'V' sign during the funeral of 28 March 2006.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted that during the demonstration held on 5 March 2007 at Dicle University, the applicant had applauded while other demonstrators chanted slogans in support of Abdullah Öcalan.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found that the funeral of 28 March 2006 and the demonstration of 5 March 2007 had subsequently turned into propaganda events in favour of the PKK and had become illegal demonstrations.
On 9 March 2007 the applicant was arrested.

The judge of the Diyarbakır Assize Court remanded the applicant in custody on the basis of a strong suspicion that he had committed the offence of disseminating propaganda in support of a terrorist organisation or its purposes.
On 8 May 2007 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor filed a bill of indictment against the applicant with the Diyarbakır Assize Court.
The applicant was charged with disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).
The applicant was charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
At the end of the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the Diyarbakır Assize Court ordered the applicant's continued detention on remand.

On 30 November 2007, at the end of the fourth hearing, the Diyarbakır Assize Court convicted the applicant of membership of an illegal organisation, the PKK, pursuant to Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court sentenced the applicant to six years and three months' imprisonment for membership of an illegal organisation, the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court convicted the applicant of two counts of disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court sentenced the applicant to a total of one year and eight months' imprisonment for two counts of disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713.

On 29 January 2009 the Court of Cassation of Turkey upheld the judgment of 30 November 2007 in so far as it related to the applicant's conviction under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code, for membership of an illegal organisation.
On 28 April 2009 the Diyarbakır Assize Court once again convicted the applicant under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (the Prevention of Terrorism Act).

On 14 December 2012 the Diyarbakır Assize Court decided to suspend the criminal proceedings against the applicant under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (the Prevention of Terrorism Act), pursuant to Law no. 6352.
The suspension of criminal proceedings against the applicant under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 was for a period of three years.

The suspension of criminal proceedings against the applicant under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 was on the condition that he did not commit an offence when expressing ideas and opinions through the medium of the press or other media, or by any other method.
After serving four years and eight months of his sentence, the applicant was released from prison on 15 November 2011.
The applicant was charged with disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).
The applicant was charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court referred to a decision dated 22 March 2007 (case no. 2006/9165, decision no. 2007/2432) of the Ninth Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation of Turkey.

In its decision of 22 March 2007, the Ninth Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation of Turkey considered that acts of accused demonstrators including participation in the demonstration of 28 March 2006 after calls by the PKK, chanting slogans in support of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan, singing the PKK's youth march song, burning tyres and blocking traffic, carrying PKK flags, banners and Öcalan posters, attacking public buildings and police and civilian vehicles with stones and Molotov cocktails, and carrying the bodies of PKK militants killed by the security forces, should be considered as offences committed on behalf of the PKK.

The Ninth Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation of Turkey found in its decision of 22 March 2007 that the accused demonstrators should be punished for those offences and also be convicted of membership of an illegal organisation.
One of the three judges sitting on the bench of the Diyarbakır Assize Court dissented from the judgment of 30 November 2007.

The dissenting judge stated that neither Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) nor the explanatory memorandum on Article 220 § 6 explained the concept of committing an offence on behalf of an illegal organisation.

The dissenting judge opined that in order to conclude that non-members of an illegal organisation had committed an offence on behalf of that illegal organisation, there should be a decision to commit an offence on behalf of that organisation and an intention to join the organisation in question.

On 29 January 2009 the Court of Cassation of Turkey upheld the judgment of 30 November 2007 in so far as it related to the applicant's conviction under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code, for membership of an illegal organisation.
On 1 April 2005 Law no. 5237 (the Criminal Code of Turkey) entered into force.

At the material time, Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who commits a crime on behalf of an illegal organisation, even if they are not a member of that organisation, shall also be punished for being a member of the organisation.

Article 314 § 1 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that anyone who forms an armed organisation to commit the crimes listed in the fourth and fifth sections of the relevant chapter, or commands such an organisation, shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of between ten and fifteen years.

Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that anyone who becomes a member of an armed organisation mentioned in Article 314 § 1 shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of between five and ten years.

Article 314 § 3 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that other provisions relating to the crime of forming an organisation for the purpose of criminal activity are also applicable for the crime of membership of an armed organisation.

On 21 February 2007 the Ninth Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation of Turkey quashed the first-instance judgment against F.Ö., holding that F.Ö.'s acts had constituted not only the offences for which he had been found guilty, but also membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3, as he had committed the offences on behalf of the organisation.

The Ninth Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation of Turkey considered that F.Ö. should be punished for the offence of membership of an illegal organisation and the other offences proscribed by section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 and section 32(1) and (3) of Law no. 2911.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted in its judgment of 31 May 2007 that in order for a court to conclude that a crime had been committed on behalf of an organisation, the latter must have issued a call for action to an individual who was capable of directly committing that act, rather than to an undefined collective group.
On 4 March 2008 the Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey decided to quash the Diyarbakır Assize Court judgment in F.Ö.'s case.

The Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey held on 4 March 2008 that participation in unauthorised demonstrations held after appeals by an illegal organisation and acts which constituted independent offences committed during those demonstrations could be considered as having been carried out on behalf of the organisation.

The Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey held on 4 March 2008 that such acts should be sanctioned under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3, along with other criminal-law provisions.

The Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey held on 4 March 2008 that appeals by an illegal organisation made in concrete terms through broadcasts by its media outlets did not need to target identified individuals.
The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that the Penal Code of Turkey does not contain a definition of an armed organisation or an armed group.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that the Court of Cassation of Turkey developed the criterion of 'membership' in an armed organisation by examining different acts of the suspect, taking account of their 'continuity, diversity and intensity' in order to see whether those acts prove an 'organic relationship' with the organisation or whether the acts may be considered as committed knowingly and wilfully within the 'hierarchical structure' of the organisation.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that if an 'organic relationship' with the organisation cannot be proven on the basis of acts attributed to the defendant which do not present any 'continuity, diversity or intensity', the paragraphs on 'aiding and abetting an armed organisation' or 'committing crime on behalf of an armed organisation' under Article 220 of the Penal Code may be applied.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that acts such as 'participating in a public demonstration following a general call from pro-PKK media outlets, making victory sign and shouting slogans to support and in favour of the leader of a terrorist organisation, clashing with the security forces and forming barricades' are considered crimes committed on behalf of an organisation and not as membership.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 recommended that the established criteria in the case law of the Court of Cassation of Turkey — that acts attributed to a defendant should show 'in their continuity, diversity and intensity' an 'organic relationship' to an organisation or prove that the defendant acted knowingly and willingly within the 'hierarchical structure' of the organisation — should be applied strictly.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that the loose application of the criteria of 'continuity, diversity and intensity' and 'organic relationship' may give rise to issues concerning in particular the principle of legality within the meaning of Article 7 of the Convention.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that the expression of an opinion in its different forms should not be the only evidence before domestic courts to decide on the membership of the defendant in an armed organisation.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that where the only evidence consists of forms of expression, a conviction for being a member of an armed organisation would constitute an interference with the right of the defendants to freedom of expression, and that the necessity of this interference should be examined in the concrete circumstances of each case on the basis of the criteria set forth in the case-law of the ECtHR, in particular the criterion of 'incitement to violence'.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that in a judgment of 4 March 2008 the General Criminal Board of the Court of Cassation of Turkey held that acts such as participating in a public demonstration following a general call from pro-PKK media outlets, making a victory sign and shouting slogans to support and in favour of the leader of a terrorist organisation, and clashing with the security forces, are considered crimes committed on behalf of the terrorist organisation.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that in the judgment of 4 March 2008, although membership in an armed organisation was not established, the defendant was convicted as a member of a criminal organisation according to Article 220 § 6 of the Penal Code applied in conjunction with Article 314.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that by the judgment of 4 March 2008, the Court of Cassation of Turkey annulled the decision of the Diyarbakır Assize Court which had considered that in order for a court to conclude that a crime was committed on behalf of an organisation, the latter must have called for action not to an undefined collective, but rather to an individual person who is capable of directly committing that act.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 recommended that the sentence 'although he is not a member of that organisation, shall also be sentenced for the offence of being a member of that organisation' in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 of the Penal Code be repealed, so that those who commit the crimes indicated in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 would not be sanctioned as members of an armed organisation under Article 314, but by other, separate sanctions.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that should the sentence in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 be maintained, the Turkish authorities should consider limiting the application of Article 220 in conjunction with Article 314 to cases which do not involve the exercise of the rights to freedom of expression and assembly.

Mr Thomas Hammarberg stated in his report of 10 January 2012 that the provisions contained in the Turkish anti-terror legislation and Article 220 of the Criminal Code of Turkey allow for a very wide margin of appreciation, in particular in cases where membership in a terrorist organisation has not been proven and when an act or statement may be deemed to coincide with the aims or instructions of a terrorist organisation.
On 28 March 2006 a funeral of four militants of the PKK (Kurdish Workers' Party), an illegal armed organisation, took place in Diyarbakır.
The crowd at the mosque on 28 March 2006 chanted separatist, hostile slogans in Turkish and Kurdish in support of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the PKK.
The crowd at the mosque on 28 March 2006 waved PKK posters and banners.
The police incident report stated that after the burial ceremony had been completed on 28 March 2006, a group of about 1,000 people continued to march.
The police warned the marching group of about 1,000 people on 28 March 2006 that they were not allowed to chant illegal slogans, disseminate propaganda in support of the PKK, or wave illegal flags.
After being warned by the police on 28 March 2006, the crowd became agitated and started throwing stones at the police officers on duty, injuring a number of them.
The crowd on 28 March 2006 caused extensive damage to State buildings and vehicles, banks, shops, and other vehicles belonging to private individuals.
According to the police incident report, more people later joined the illegal demonstration, which continued on 29, 30 and 31 March and 1 April 2006.
On 5 March 2007 a demonstration was held on the campus of Dicle University to protest about the conditions of Abdullah Öcalan's detention.
The demonstration on 5 March 2007 at Dicle University protested in particular about the alleged poisoning of Abdullah Öcalan by the Turkish authorities.
On 5 March 2007 the group of forty people chanted slogans in favour of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan on the premises of Dicle University.

The applicant was charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had attended the funeral on 28 March 2006 as a religious duty.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had not attacked the police with stones during the events of 28 March 2006.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that on 5 March 2007 he had stood in front of the Dicle University building with other students for a short while.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that his photograph must have been taken while he stood in front of the Dicle University building on 5 March 2007.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had not chanted slogans with the demonstrators on 5 March 2007.

At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant denied the accuracy of the allegation that he had chanted slogans during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant denied the accuracy of the allegation that he had chanted slogans during the demonstration of 5 March 2007.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant stated that he did not remember making a 'V' sign but that he might have done so along with the rest of the crowd.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, a witness was heard by the Diyarbakır Assize Court and confirmed the applicant's version of events of 5 March 2007.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed, on the basis of the police video recordings and photographs extracted from those recordings, that the applicant had attended the funeral of four PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had walked in front of one of the coffins during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had made a 'V' sign during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted that it was not established that the applicant had chanted slogans during the funeral of 28 March 2006.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted that during the demonstration held on 5 March 2007 at Dicle University, the applicant had applauded while other demonstrators chanted slogans in support of Abdullah Öcalan.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found that the funeral of 28 March 2006 and the demonstration of 5 March 2007 had subsequently turned into propaganda events in favour of the PKK and had become illegal demonstrations.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found it established that the applicant had acted with the intention of supporting the deceased PKK militants on 28 March 2006, thereby committing the offence of disseminating propaganda in favour of the PKK and its leader.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found it established that the applicant had acted together with illegal demonstrators on 5 March 2007, thereby committing the offence of disseminating propaganda in favour of the PKK and its leader.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant's participation in the funeral and demonstration of 28 March 2006 and his conduct at that time had occurred as a result of instructions and calls by the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant had acted on behalf of the PKK, in line with the goals and activities of the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant should be punished not only for disseminating propaganda but also for membership of an illegal organisation.
One of the three judges sitting on the bench of the Diyarbakır Assize Court dissented from the judgment of 30 November 2007.

The dissenting judge stated that neither Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) nor the explanatory memorandum on Article 220 § 6 explained the concept of committing an offence on behalf of an illegal organisation.

The dissenting judge noted that an offence committed on behalf of an illegal organisation should be capable of producing a result for a terrorist organisation and its aims, such as the offences of aggravated injury, kidnapping, deprivation of liberty, murder or bombing.

The dissenting judge noted that an offence committed on behalf of an illegal organisation should have devastating repercussions for society when the way of committing the offence, the time of the offence and its effects were taken into consideration.

The dissenting judge opined that in order to conclude that non-members of an illegal organisation had committed an offence on behalf of that illegal organisation, there should be a decision to commit an offence on behalf of that organisation and an intention to join the organisation in question.
The dissenting judge concluded that the applicant should only have been convicted under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (the Prevention of Terrorism Act).
On 25 October 2010 the applicant was expelled from Dicle University by the administrative board of the Faculty of Arts and Science.
The applicant was expelled from Dicle University because he had failed to complete his degree within the maximum period of seven years for an undergraduate programme.
The Diyarbakır Administrative Court considered that the fact that the applicant had been serving a prison sentence did not justify his non-attendance at classes and examinations.
After serving four years and eight months of his sentence, the applicant was released from prison on 15 November 2011.

According to the new paragraph added to section 7 of Law no. 3713 by Law no. 6459, people who have committed the offence under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation) shall not in addition be held criminally liable under Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

According to the new paragraph added to section 7 of Law no. 3713 by Law no. 6459, people who have committed the offence under section 28(1) of the Marches and Demonstrations Act (Law no. 2911) (participating in an unlawful demonstration) shall not in addition be held criminally liable under Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 welcomed the amendment introduced to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713, which excluded the above-mentioned crimes from the scope of application of Article 220(6) of the Penal Code.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 considered that the scope of the amendment to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713 is rather limited and does not provide for sufficient protection to the exercise of freedom of expression and assembly.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 recommended that the sentence 'although he is not a member of that organisation, shall also be sentenced for the offence of being a member of that organisation' in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 of the Penal Code be repealed, so that those who commit the crimes indicated in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 would not be sanctioned as members of an armed organisation under Article 314, but by other, separate sanctions.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that should the sentence in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 be maintained, the Turkish authorities should consider limiting the application of Article 220 in conjunction with Article 314 to cases which do not involve the exercise of the rights to freedom of expression and assembly.

In a report published on 10 January 2012 following a visit to Turkey between 10 and 14 October 2011, Mr Thomas Hammarberg, the former Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that any allegation of terrorist activity must be established with convincing evidence and beyond any reasonable doubt.

Mr Thomas Hammarberg stated in his report of 10 January 2012 that violence or the threat to use violence is an essential component of an act of terrorism, and that restrictions of human rights in the fight against terrorism must be defined as precisely as possible and be necessary and proportionate to the aim pursued.

Mr Thomas Hammarberg stated in his report of 10 January 2012 that the provisions contained in the Turkish anti-terror legislation and Article 220 of the Criminal Code of Turkey allow for a very wide margin of appreciation, in particular in cases where membership in a terrorist organisation has not been proven and when an act or statement may be deemed to coincide with the aims or instructions of a terrorist organisation.
